findings.title: Worker and WASM adapters wrap pim values of 2^32 and above instead of rejecting them
findings.evidence: Node.js probe: new MhfeEngine(4294967296) reports pim 0; new MhfeEngine(4294967327) reports pim 31 / effectivePasses 384; decryptJson(container, 4294967308) executes as 12 words. Generated glue passes numbers to i32 parameters without range checks; Worker requireInteger accepts any non-negative safe integer.
findings.reproduction: initSync the dist; call new MhfeEngine(2**32) and read engine.pim; call decryptJson(container, 2**32+12) with a staged password.
findings.expected: Every adapter rejects pim outside 0..31 with INVALID_PIM and sourceWords outside {12,15,18,21,24} with INVALID_SOURCE_WORDS.
findings.observed: Values >= 2^32 are reduced modulo 2^32 and executed; the Worker guards sourceWords but not pim; direct WASM callers are unguarded for both.
findings.impact: A caller with an out-of-range PIM silently gets a container at a different work factor; the returned pim field allows detection; the Rust core is correct.
findings.recommendedFix: Bound pim to 0..maxPim in web/mhfe-worker.js ensureEngine and in web/client.js; document integer-range responsibility for direct WASM callers; add a Node test for 2**32.
findings.requiredVerification: Worker rejects 2**32 and 2**32+31 with INVALID_PIM; PIM 0..31 still pass; boundary covered by verify-wasm-api.mjs or a new test.

findings.title: Browser operational exports have no automated runtime check; local build is stale
findings.evidence: verify-wasm-api.mjs checks only suite parameters and PIM 32; diff web/*.js dist/*.js shows dist lacks decryptAuto paths; dist/wasm/mhfe.d.ts has no decryptAutoJson; measurements/local-browser-pim-0.json predates automatic detection.
findings.reproduction: diff web/client.js dist/client.js; grep decryptAuto dist/wasm/mhfe.d.ts; read scripts/verify-wasm-api.mjs.
findings.expected: At least one automated check executes encryptJson, decryptJson and decryptAutoJson of the generated WASM; recorded browser evidence corresponds to the source it describes.
findings.observed: No operational export is executed by any automated check; the automatic-detection path has no runtime evidence in any browser build; the stale binary still reproduces the published container under Node.js.
findings.impact: A regression confined to the wasm-bindgen boundary of the operational exports would pass CI.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a real PIM 0 round trip (about 90 s under Node.js) to verify-wasm-api.mjs or a CI step; rebuild dist with scripts/build-wasm.sh and re-record the browser measurement using the automatic-detection path.
findings.requiredVerification: CI log shows the round trip; dist/wasm/mhfe.d.ts contains decryptAutoJson; measurement file names its source fingerprint.

findings.title: Security-reporting channel named in SECURITY.md is not enabled; specification unlinked
findings.evidence: GET /repos/hobby-eng/mhfe/private-vulnerability-reporting returns {"enabled": false} (same for mhfe-spec); README has no link to the specification repository; repository was 404 at the start of the review and public after the push.
findings.reproduction: Query the private-vulnerability-reporting endpoint unauthenticated; search README.md for a specification URL.
findings.expected: The channel named in SECURITY.md is enabled; README links the companion specification.
findings.observed: Private vulnerability reporting disabled; Cargo.toml URL now resolves; specification repository unlinked.
findings.impact: A reporter following SECURITY.md cannot open a private advisory; the release workflow packages SECURITY.md into archives.
findings.recommendedFix: Enable private vulnerability reporting (both repositories) or name an alternative private channel; link https://github.com/hobby-eng/mhfe-spec from README.md.
findings.requiredVerification: Endpoint returns {"enabled": true}; README link resolves.

observations.title: Verifier and fixed-point comparisons are not constant-time
observations.evidence: src/lib.rs 723 and 776 use != and == on verifier and state bytes.
observations.expected: No requirement in the threat model; noted for reuse elsewhere.
observations.observed: Non-constant-time comparisons on values the container holder can compute.
observations.impact: None for the current threat model; Argon2id timing dominates.

observations.title: Terminating a client before ready() is observed leaves an unhandled rejection
observations.evidence: web/client.js rejects #ready from terminate/cancel/error handlers; no internal handler attached.
observations.reproduction: Construct a client and call cancel() before awaiting ready().
observations.observed: Internal promise rejects unobserved; console noise only.
observations.recommendedFix: Attach a no-op catch to #ready while returning the original promise from ready().

observations.title: Wrong password under automatic detection returns an unverified 24-word result
observations.evidence: CLI probe: wrong password without --source-words exits 0 with Detected source words 24 and Recovery verified false; with --source-words 12 exits 1 with RECOVERY_VERIFIER_MISMATCH.
observations.reproduction: Decrypt the published 12-word container with a wrong password, with and without --source-words.
observations.expected: Specified fallback behaviour; consumers must surface the unverified flag.
observations.observed: Behaves as specified across CLI, Rust, WASM and Worker results.
observations.impact: A consumer that ignores recovery_verified / recoveryVerifier could present garbage as a recovered phrase.
observations.recommendedFix: Print an explicit warning line on the unverified CLI path; keep the flag prominent in consumers.

observations.title: actions/checkout is tag-pinned while the audit action is SHA-pinned
observations.evidence: Four workflows use actions/checkout@v4; audit action pinned to 72c09e02.
observations.recommendedFix: Pin checkout to a SHA with a version comment; Dependabot keeps it updated.
